6258.text: In Rom.2.7 zeteo (kath' hupomonen ergou agathou doxan... zetousin) sits within its base gloss of diligent pursuit/striving toward a good end -- no unusual nuance beyond the standard 'seek/strive for' sense used elsewhere for pursuing eschatological goods.

6259.text: The operation word zeteo ('seek') is directed by 'those who' (the subject party, believers described by patient well-doing) toward the object 'glory and honor and immortality' -- the seeking party initiates the action toward the divine reward, not toward another person.

6260.text: Seeking (G2212) here functions as the operative disposition that yields glory (M22), honor (M71), and immortality (M61) via well-doing (M05) and patience (M34) and eternal life (M25); seeking is the pursuit-verb binding these other characteristics together as the sought objects/means, giving the first relational read of this verse's M-code cluster.

7015.text: Ps.119.45's 'I have sought your precepts' fits the base gloss's sense of seeking/enquiring with application (1a7), consistent with its use in v.94; no distinguishing nuance beyond standard devotional seeking.

7020.text: Ps.119.45 also contains M08 (wide place, H7342H). The wide place is the resultant condition of walking freely, not something sought directly by darash; seeking precepts is the ground and cause of the freedom described, but the two M-codes describe distinct elements (act of seeking vs. resulting spaciousness).

15719.text: G0073 (agōn) is not a vice at all but a positive athletic and military metaphor for perseverance. Every one of its 6 verses is Paul or Hebrews describing his own or the believer's faithful effort: fight the good fight of the faith (1 Tim 6:12), I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race (2 Tim 4:7), run with endurance the race that is set before us (Heb 12:1). Nothing in this strong's verse set describes wrongdoing, discord or a moral failure of any kind; its inclusion in the cluster looks like a gloss-text accident (the English word fight) and not a thematic match, a candidate for a cluster_strong review.

15802.text: G0073 (agon) has real, coherent, human-relevant meaning: a struggle or contest, most often used in the NT as an athletic or perseverance metaphor for faithful endurance: fight the good fight of the faith (1 Tim 6:12), I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race (2 Tim 4:7), run with endurance the race that is set before us (Heb 12:1). None of its 6 occurrences describes a moral failure or an inner disposition toward wrongdoing.

18875.text: *Ṭāman*, "to hide, bury". A thing is put into or under something. Achan's plunder is "hidden in the earth inside my tent" (Joshua 7:21). Moses "hid him in the sand" (Exodus 2:12). An enemy's net is hidden in the path (Psalm 140:5). It is also the word for the sluggard who "buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth" (Proverbs 19:24).

18883.text: Hiding what I hold: A person can hide what he has done. Achan tells it in order: "when I saw … then I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the earth inside my tent" (Joshua 7:21). Joshua had to ask him first: "do not hide it from me" (7:19).; What happens next differs.

18889.text: The hidden trap: In the Psalms a purpose is hidden in order to catch someone. "They hold fast to their evil purpose; they talk of laying snares secretly, thinking, 'Who can see them?'" (Psalm 64:5). The next verse says where the purpose was hidden first: "For the inward mind and heart of a man are deep" (64:6).; The one it is set for prays out of his weakness. "When my spirit faints within me, you know my way! In the path where I walk they have hidden a trap for me" (Psalm 142:3). "No one cares for my soul" (142:4). It is worse when it comes from those he had prayed for: "Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them" (Jeremiah 18:20).; And the trap turns. "In the net that they hid, their own foot has been caught" (Psalm 9:15). The soul the pit was dug for (Psalm 35:7) is the soul that rejoices: "Then my soul will rejoice in the Lord" (35:9). The one taken "out of the net they have hidden for me" says, "Into your hand I commit my spirit" (Psalm 31:4–5).

18927.text: *taman* H2934, hide (27) | Psa 35:7 "a pit for my life"; Psa 142:3 "my spirit faints … they have hidden a trap" | Hidden traps: Psa 9:15; 31:4; 35:8; 140:5; Job 18:10; Jer 18:22. The seat is the victim's life or spirit | Objects hidden (Gen 35:4; Jos 2:6; Jer 13; 43). Two notes: Jos 7:21 has coveting (M18) followed by hiding, and Pro 19:24 / 26:15, "the sluggard buries his hand in the dish", shows inertia of will carried by the hand

18930.text: *de'agah* H1674 / *da'ag* H1672, anxiety (11) | Pro 12:25 "Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down" | Anxiety enacted in eating and drinking: Eze 4:16; 12:18–19 ("eat your bread with quaking … drink water with trembling and with anxiety"). The body carries it. The image carries it in Jer 17:8 (a tree "not anxious in the year of drought"), framed by 17:5 ("whose heart turns away") and 17:9–10 ("The heart is deceitful … I the Lord search the heart") | 1Sa 9:5; 10:2: a father's anxiety, carried by his spoken question ("What shall I do about my son?"). The sense shifts in Psa 38:18, "I am sorry for my sin": anxiety turned to repentance

19272.text: What it does to the one it is set for. "When my spirit faints within me, you know my way! In the path where I walk they have hidden a trap for me" (Psa 142:3). The next verse: "no one cares for my soul" (142:4). The trap is aimed at "my life" (35:7).

19288.text: Jos 7:19–22: seeing → coveting → taking → hiding → demand to disclose → confession → found

20555.text: Face: A growl, and its absence; Verses: Isa 31:4; Psa 115:7; Isa 8:19; What differs: God as a lion growling over his prey, "not terrified" (protective); idols that "do not make a sound in their throat"; mediums who "mutter"

21499.text: Uprightly gives a moral condition to what it binds (an upright heart, a righteous or wicked way, godly grief, walking uprightly, a sinful nation): the uprightness, godliness or wickedness of the heart, speech, way or conduct.

21510.text: Wickedness here describes a thing or a figure (a sinful thing, a wicked scheme only as an object); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
